subtopics.title: Plot exponential graphs
subtopics.exposition: The exponential functions y = f(x) = b^x are defined for b > 0 and b ≠ 1. All the graphs of y = b^x (here b = 2, 3 and 5) pass through the point (0, 1). The y-intercept is the point (0, 1) for all the graphs of y = (1/b)^x (here b = 2, 3 and 5) as well. For any real number z not equal to 0, z^0 = 1, which is why the graphs of y = b^x all pass through (0, 1). The graphs of y = b^x do not cut the x-axis, because you can never get 0 by raising any non-zero number to the power of any other number. The equation of the horizontal asymptote of the graphs of y = b^x and y = (1/b)^x is y = 0, the x-axis. As x increases, h(x) = 5^x increases. Of f(x) = 2^x, g(x) = 3^x and h(x) = 5^x, f(x) = 2^x increases at the slowest rate because it has the smallest base. For y = k^x with k > 1, the greater the value of k, the steeper the graph. The graph of F(x) = (1/2)^x is the reflection of the graph of f(x) = 2^x about the y-axis. The graph of G(x) = (1/3)^x is the reflection of the graph of g(x) = 3^x about the y-axis. For y = (1/k)^x with k > 1, the greater the value of k, the steeper the graph. To complete a table of values for y = b^x, substitute the values of x into the equations. Graphs of exponential functions with different values of b are drawn on the same system of axes. To draw the graph, plot the points from the table and join them with a smooth curve. To investigate the effect of b, plot graphs on the same set of axes with a = 1 and q = 0 so that only b changes, then use the results to deduce the effect of b.

subtopics.title: Determine equation from graph
subtopics.exposition: Functions of the general form y = ab^x + q are called exponential functions. The effect of q is called a vertical shift, because all points are moved the same distance in the same direction (it slides the entire graph up or down). For q > 0, the graph is shifted vertically upwards by q units. For q < 0, the graph is shifted vertically downwards by q units. The sign of a determines whether the graph curves upwards or downwards. For b > 1 and a > 0, the graph curves upwards. For b > 1 and a < 0, the graph curves downwards; it reflects the graph about the horizontal asymptote. To investigate the effect of q, plot graphs on the same set of axes with b = 2 and a = 1 so that only q changes, then use the results to deduce the effect of q. To investigate the effect of a, plot graphs on the same set of axes with b = 2 and q = 0 so that only a changes, then use the results to deduce the effect of a. In y = ab^x + q, a and q are constants and have different effects on the function.

subtopics.title: Domain and range
subtopics.exposition: For y = b^x with b > 0 and b ≠ 1, the domain is all real x and the range is {y: y in R, y > 0}. For y = ab^x + q, the function is defined for all real values of x, so the domain is {x: x in R}. The range of y = ab^x + q depends on the sign of a. For a > 0, the range is {f(x): f(x) > q}. For a < 0, the range is {f(x): f(x) < q}. To find the range when a > 0: b^x > 0, so ab^x > 0, so ab^x + q > q, so f(x) > q. To find the range when a < 0: b^x > 0, so ab^x < 0, so ab^x + q < q, so f(x) < q. For g(x) = 5·2^x + 1: 2^x > 0, so 5×2^x > 0, so 5×2^x + 1 > 1; therefore the range is {g(x): g(x) > 1} and the domain is all real x. The standard form of an exponential function is y = ab^x + q.

subtopics.title: Calculate intercepts
subtopics.exposition: The y-intercept of y = ab^x + q is a + q, because b^0 = 1. If setting y = 0 gives no real solution (for g(x) = 5×2^x + 1 it gives 2^x = -1/5), the graph does not have any x-intercepts. For g(x) = 3×2^x + 2, setting y = 0 gives 2^x = -2/3, which has no real solution, therefore there is no x-intercept. For the y-intercept, let x = 0. For g(x) = 5×2^x + 1, setting x = 0 gives 5 + 1 = 6, so the y-intercept is the point (0, 6). For the x-intercept, let y = 0. For y = -2×3^x + 6, setting y = 0 gives 3^1 = 3^x, so x = 1 and the x-intercept is the point (1, 0).

subtopics.title: Sketch exponential graphs
subtopics.exposition: The horizontal asymptote of y = ab^x + q is shifted by q units and is the line y = q. Exponential functions of the form y = ab^x + q have a single horizontal asymptote. To sketch the graph of y = ab^x + q, four characteristics must be determined. The four characteristics needed to sketch y = ab^x + q are the sign of a, the y-intercept, the x-intercept and the asymptote. Step 1 of sketching: examine the standard form of the equation, using the sign of a to decide whether the graph curves upwards or downwards and the value of q to decide the vertical shift. Step 2 of sketching: calculate the intercepts (y-intercept with x = 0, x-intercept with y = 0). Step 3 of sketching: determine the asymptote, the horizontal line y = q (for g(x) = 3×2^x + 2 it is y = 2). Step 4 of sketching: plot the points and sketch the graph. A sketch of an exponential graph marks the intercept and the asymptote.
